page: Microsoft Azure D96s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, featuring 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It is powered by an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz, backed by an extensive cache hierarchy that includes a 480 MB L3 cache and 2 MB of L2 cache per core. The instance is provisioned with 384 GB of memory, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. It does not include integrated GPUs or bundled local storage, requiring network-attached remote storage volumes for persistent data.

The CPU architecture incorporates advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512, Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), and hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions like VAES and SHA-NI. In benchmark testing, the large core count and massive L3 cache yield strong multi-threaded throughput. It achieved a top-tier PassMark CPU score of 105,569.39 and demonstrated strong decompression throughput with bzip3 reaching 556.8 GB/sec. Memory subsystem benchmarks show high cached read bandwidth of 7,051.06 GB/sec and uncached read bandwidth of 345.73 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput workloads like in-memory key-value processing, where Redis reached 152.07 million SET operations per second.

Without included ephemeral or scratch disks, all IO must transit the network, making overall system throughput dependent on attached premium storage tiers. However, the high compute density and vector acceleration enable capable matrix and integer operations, reflected in solid prompt-processing rates across LLM benchmark tests. The machine profile is well matched for compute-heavy web tiers, large-scale software compilation, distributed database engines, and parallel batch data processing.
description: Microsoft Azure D96s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 96 dedicated vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at 4.2 GHz. The instance features a 480 MB L3 cache, advanced instruction support including AVX-512 and AMX, and 384 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 4 GB per vCPU allocation. There are no bundled local storage disks or GPUs, meaning all persistence relies on remote block storage. In benchmark evaluations, the D96s_v7 exhibits top-tier multi-threaded compute and memory bandwidth, scoring 105,569.39 in PassMark CPU and recording 152.07 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. Its processing capacity and large cache hierarchy make it suitable for large-scale multi-threaded workloads, in-memory caching layers, compilation pipelines, and enterprise application servers.
